ov: Sea snails with a cone-shaped shell and a strong muscular foot that clamps them to rocks on the shore. At high tide they wander and graze algae with a tongue of iron-hardened teeth, then follow their own mucus trail back to their favourite spot.

why.et: Eaten in Portugal (lapas) and Asturias in Spain; in Ireland it was famine food, so tough it had to be boiled or roasted thoroughly.

len: Common limpet up to about 6 cm
df: Algae scraped off rocks with its radula, a tongue with over 100 rows of teeth.
fx: Over time its shell wears a shallow hollow, a "homescar", into the rock where it rests.
Worn teeth are thrown away as new ones grow, about one new row every 47 hours.
